Port strike ends after 12 days as workers accept pay deal

By Jane Doe, Business reporter

30 October 2026
Share on Facebook Share on X Email

Dock workers at the port of Northhaven have voted to accept a 9% pay rise, ending a 12-day strike that left hundreds of containers stranded and delayed deliveries across the region.

The union said 78% of members backed the offer in a ballot that closed on Wednesday evening, with a turnout of 64%. Work will resume on the night shift on Thursday.

Advertisement

What the deal includes

  • A 9% pay rise backdated to July
  • A one-off payment of 1,500 for every worker
  • A review of shift patterns within six months

Port operator Northhaven Docks said it was “pleased that an agreement has been reached” and that the backlog of about 4,000 containers would be cleared within a fortnight.

Retailers had warned that the dispute, the longest at the port since 1998, threatened supplies of electronics and clothing in the run-up to the holiday season.
